works.title: The Blind Spot
works.inspired_by: Modern Metro and Meta Quest 3 spec-poster references
works.prompt: Cinematic product photography of a precision-machined exploded assembly in a deep near-black void. Five turned discs on one axis - anodised graphite aluminium, brushed titanium collars, black ceramic inserts, concentric machining marks. FOUR are sealed, each with a continuous cold-cyan seam of light around its circumference. THE THIRD FROM TOP IS BREACHED: a clean circular void punched through, chamfered edges, nothing inside, no cyan seam, inner bore rimmed in hot amber with the glow spilling onto its neighbours. The hole is the focal point. 100mm macro at f/8, one high softbox left plus two rim strips, faint volumetric haze, true blacks, no lifted greys. Palette strictly near-black, graphite, brushed steel, cold cyan, one hot amber. Generous empty black margins top, bottom and both sides, reserved for type. Absolutely no lettering, numerals, engraved marks, serials, logos or dial markings anywhere - all type is composited afterwards in HTML.
works.takeaway: You bought a managed guardrail. It does not read toolUse.input, toolResult or toolSpec - so the one station where an agent can actually cause harm is the one nothing inspects.

works.title: Where Guardrails Go in an AI Application
works.prompt: Blueprint Ledger style-DNA - blueprint indigo (#1f3a5f) on warm paper, Georgia display, mono spec labels, single-weight line-art on a ruled grid. Hero is a hand-authored inline SVG schematic, not diffusion: a greyed UNGUARDED baseline lane across the top, then three bands - input guard, the LLM application with dashed guard capsules at retrieval and tool call, and output guard - with a stream-guard capsule on the return wire and fail branches labelled block, redact, reask. Rendered with Chrome headless at A4 portrait.
works.takeaway: Alignment lowers the base rate, guardrails cap the tail, evals tell you whether either works. A system prompt does none of the three - and on Bedrock the managed guardrail never reads the tool call.

works.title: You approved the number. You inherited the shadow.
works.inspired_by: Constructed-object poster photography and measured forecast fan charts
works.concept: Executive forecasts often collapse a distribution into one approved number; the missing interval becomes the operating risk the business inherits.
works.prompt:
DESIGN-BUILT (not prompted) - hand-authored HTML/SVG, rendered with Chrome.
STYLE: graphic measured-shadow poster. A signed point-estimate card sits on a diagonal planning axis and casts a widening prediction-interval fan across a ruled quarterly horizon.
MARKS: point card = approved forecast value; dark widening fan = uncertainty over time; diagonal grid = forecast horizon; acid-lime marker = where the actual business commitment lands; lamp/assumption set = the model assumptions casting the range.
PALETTE: warm planning-paper ground, near-black ink and graphite interval bands, one acid-lime accent only for the downstream commitment.
TYPE: compressed heavy sans for the warning, monospace labels for the forecast system, tabular numerals on the point estimate.
MESSAGE: approve the range, not just the value.
works.takeaway: A forecast is a distribution. Removing the interval does not remove the risk - it only moves the risk to the operator.

works.title: The accuracy mask
works.concept: A polished validation score can become a public mask when the evidence behind it is empty, synthetic, or meaningless.
works.prompt: Create a vivid, bold editorial image about a data model that displays a perfect board-ready score while secretly being validated on fake data that means nothing. Avoid literal robots and corporate stock-photo cliches. Concept/metaphor: A giant glossy green "97%" approval mask floats on a vivid orange-pink background like a perfect public face. Behind the mask, the back side is peeled open in an X-ray / paper-cutaway collage, exposing that the mask is stuffed with hundreds of identical blank grey placeholder cards. The blank cards spill downward like a waterfall into an empty black void. Small applauding executive silhouettes appear only as tiny paper cutouts at the bottom, dwarfed by the score-mask. Style/medium: bold editorial paper collage mixed with screenprint, vivid color blocking, sharp surreal magazine cover, tactile torn-paper edges, high contrast, graphic and memorable. Think art-director poster energy, not dashboard art. Composition/framing: 4:5 portrait. Huge central 97% mask takes most of the frame. Peeled-open backside and blank-card stuffing must be obvious. Strong negative space around the main object. Bottom silhouettes are tiny and secondary. Mood: electric and uneasy - confidence as a mask, truth as hollow stuffing. Color palette: saturated vermilion, magenta, acid green, ink black, bone white, blank neutral grey. Bold but disciplined, no rainbow clutter. Text (verbatim): only "97%" as the face of the mask. No caption, no extra readable text. Constraints: The blank grey cards must read as meaningless fake validation inputs. The 97% must feel polished and seductive. Avoid robots, sci-fi circuitry, generic dashboards, boardroom photo realism, logos, watermark, extra text, horror gore, and cute mascots.
works.takeaway: A perfect score is not proof. Validation only means something when the validation data means something.

works.title: The average customer is a myth
works.concept: Averages can turn many incompatible customer realities into one fake persona, hiding where margin, churn, support cost, and discounting actually live.
works.prompt: Create an unforgettable portrait 4:5 editorial poster titled exactly "THE AVERAGE CUSTOMER IS A MYTH". Show a pristine museum gallery where a beautiful white marble statue labeled "AVERAGE CUSTOMER" is cracking apart. Inside the cracks are not bones or machinery but hundreds of tiny mismatched customer receipts, invoices, support tickets, discount tags, churn notes, premium badges, and margin slips spilling out in different colors and sizes. One elegant executive stands in front of the statue with a confident presentation card reading exactly "AVG +8%", unaware that the statue is hollow and impossible. The visual message: the average customer is a fake artifact assembled from customers who do not behave alike. Premium museum editorial set, quiet off-white walls, soft gallery lighting, expensive magazine-cover art direction, strong negative space. Luxury editorial surrealism, sculptural realism mixed with crisp graphic data ephemera, publication-grade typography, subtle paper grain, refined not flashy. Centered statue as hero, title at top with clean generous margin, executive small at lower left for scale, fragments spilling diagonally to create motion. Warm ivory, charcoal ink, marble white, muted teal shadows, restrained red for loss notes, small green accent on AVG card. Render exactly and clearly: "THE AVERAGE CUSTOMER IS A MYTH"; "AVERAGE CUSTOMER"; "AVG +8%". No other text. No visible charts, histograms, dashboards, robots, brains, network nodes, generic AI glow, stock corporate illustration, cluttered labels, extra text, watermark, living artist imitation, or brand mimicry.
works.takeaway: The average customer is a myth - decide on the distribution, not the mean.

works.title: The model can't spell strawberry
works.inspired_by: Two-color system - OFF+BRAND (Lando Norris) x Josef Müller-Brockmann
works.prompt: Flat vector editorial data-portrait poster, crop 4:5. STRICT two-color system: acid lime #D2FF00 and near-black #111112 ONLY - no white, no gray, no third color, no gradients. Near-black background. Concept: an LLM confidently miscounts letters because it reads tokens, not characters. HERO: a giant acid-lime '2' (the model's confident answer) with a bold strike-through slash, and a smaller correct '3' beside it. Top-left, tiny mono-caps question: 'HOW MANY R'S IN STRAWBERRY?'. Below the hero, the word 'strawberry' broken into token tiles [str][aw][berry], with the three r's circled inside the tiles so the eye hunts and finds them. Bottom: one thin acid-lime hairline rule with caption 'It reads tokens, not letters. That's why it can't spell.' Massive negative space, Swiss grid discipline, the joke lands in two seconds. No logos, no watermark, no photoreal, flat only.
works.takeaway: LLMs read tokens, not letters - which is why they confidently miscount the r's in strawberry. The unit of thought isn't the character you see.

works.title: The AI landscape
works.concept: The field of AI drawn as a metro - six lines you can trace end to end, with interchange stations marking exactly where two disciplines share an idea.
works.prompt:
DESIGN-BUILT (not prompted) - hand-authored SVG, rendered headless.
STYLE: transit map, Vignelli discipline - cream ground, one bold colour per line, uniform station dots, stadium interchange markers, 45/90 geometry, Helvetica.
LINES: Machine Learning · Deep Learning · Language · Vision · Generative & Agents · Data & MLOps (the full-width foundation everything rides on).
INTERCHANGES (where fields connect): Neural Networks = ML + Deep Learning · Embeddings = Deep Learning + Language · Transformers = Language + Vision + Generative.
Full editable SVG source is published alongside this work as sheet.html.
works.takeaway: The whole field is one connected network - and the breakthroughs happen at the interchanges (embeddings, transformers), all riding on data. Most people never leave their home station.

works.title: RAG vs Fine-tuning vs Prompt-tuning
works.prompt: Blueprint Ledger style-DNA - deep blueprint indigo (#1f3a5f) on warm paper, Georgia display + mono spec labels, thin ruled hairlines. Hero: four LLM levers as blueprint line-art (prompt box, RAG retrieval circle, fine-tune dial, soft-prompt vectors). Rendered SVG, not diffusion.
works.takeaway: Fine-tuning teaches a skill; RAG supplies facts. Default to prompt + RAG - fine-tune only the pipelines that prove they need it.

works.title: The minds of modern AI
works.concept: Modern AI emerged when learning ideas met data, compute, and engineering - but its pioneers still disagree about the road to human-level intelligence.
works.prompt: Portrait storybook editorial infographic titled “THE MINDS OF MODERN AI,” using an airy cream paper background, watercolor-and-gouache textures, delicate ink outlines, light pastel colors, and a winding golden path through four chapters: “1 · BREAKTHROUGHS” showing Bengio, Dally, Hinton, Huang, Li, and LeCun with their core contributions; “2 · AI BUBBLE?” contrasting real value today with the limits of the current paradigm; “3 · HUMAN-LEVEL AI” presenting six divergent views through signposts and an airplane-and-bird metaphor; and “4 · THE SHARED LESSON” ending in a collaborative human-and-machine library-city with the banners “BUILD USEFUL SYSTEMS,” “EXPLORE BEYOND LANGUAGE,” and “GOVERN BEFORE ACCELERATION.” Premium, vivid, optimistic, intellectually serious, readable, no logos, no watermark, no dark cyberpunk, no corporate stock-art look.
works.takeaway: AI's practical value is already real; what remains uncertain is whether scale, new paradigms, or human-machine collaboration defines the road ahead.
